key_insight: Moving the elastic axis aft closes the folded transonic flutter boundary by reducing supersonic-surface damping faster than the residual shock energy input.
engineering_relevance: Elastic-axis placement can determine whether multiple flutter-speed thresholds coexist at one Mach number, complicating aeroelastic stability assessment.
method: Coupled unsteady Euler simulations of a pitch–plunge aerofoil with varying elastic-axis position.
Batch active learning of a Gaussian-process damping surrogate, calibrated using independent split conformal prediction.
Chordwise energy budgets to explain shock-driven energy transfer and fold closure.
evidence_signal: With 80 simulations, the case A model correctly labeled 64 of 65 independent runs; a broader study using 193 simulations and 40 calibration runs placed fold closure between 0.39 and 0.33 chord ahead of the leading edge on two meshes.
watch_item: Results concern inviscid flow, and time-domain damping labels require careful checks: the common one-degree start left a mean incidence that raised dip flutter speed by 2.8%.
paper_title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
